title: FactorIA ENGINE_FEEDBACK.json
description: Log of things the FactorIA engine lacked while building this game, and how the author (usually an AI) worked around them. Engine developers aggregate these files with `factoria feedback collect` to decide what to build next. Append entries with the `feedback.report` command (MCP tool `feedback_report`) rather than editing by hand.

project.description: Name of the game project this file belongs to (factoria.json "name").

engineVersion.description: Engine version the project was made with, e.g. "0.1.0".

nextId.description: The number the next new id gets at least. Written when an entry is deleted, so its id is not given again.

entries.description: Feedback entries, oldest first. Ids are FB-0001, FB-0002, ... and never reused.

category.description: Engine area the gap belongs to.

severity.description: blocker: the game (or a requested feature) could not be built at all. major: needed a large or fragile workaround. minor: small workaround. nice-to-have: would be more convenient.

status.description: Lifecycle: open (default), fixed-in-engine, wont-fix, duplicate, rejected (the entry claims a gap the engine does not have: see statusReason). Entries that are not open move to the archive file.

kind.description: Whether an AI agent or a person reported it.

model.description: Model id when kind is ai, e.g. "claude-sonnet-5-5".

entry.description: One engine gap and the workaround used.

id.description: Stable id, FB-0001 style. Assigned automatically.

date.description: UTC date the entry was first written, YYYY-MM-DD.

title.description: Short noun phrase naming the gap, e.g. "No fluid simulation" (an invented example). Reuse the same wording for the same gap so entries can be grouped.

missing.description: What exactly the engine lacked or got wrong, and what you were trying to do.

workaround.description: What you did instead (or "none: feature dropped"). Be concrete so engine developers can judge the cost.

workaroundFiles.description: Project-relative files that implement the workaround.

suggestion.description: How the engine could fix it (component field, command, API), as specific as possible.

effort.description: Reporter's estimate of the engine-side effort to fix it.

occurrences.description: How many times this gap was hit/reported. Incremented when a similar open entry is reported again.

distinctFrom.description: Ids of entries this one is a different gap from ("FB-0011", or "<project>/FB-0011" for another project's). `feedback collect` never puts them in one group, however alike the titles are.

notes.description: Extra workaround descriptions from repeated reports, each prefixed with its date.

statusReason.description: Why the status is what it is: required with rejected (what exists, where it is documented), optional with wont-fix and duplicate. Plain text, shown to the person in the editor. Removed when the entry is opened again.

statusBy.description: Who set a closed status: engine (the check found that the claimed gap already exists), user (a person or the AI of the project), developer (the engine developer rejected the shared report).

claimCheck.description: dismissed: a person reopened an entry the engine had rejected, so the engine never rejects it again.

suggestedRejection.description: On entries pulled from the feedback server (engine developer only): `factoria feedback pull` found that the report calls missing something the engine already has, and suggests rejecting it with this reason. Confirm with `factoria feedback reject --suggested`, or drop it with `factoria feedback keep`.

reason.description: The ready reason: what exists and where it is documented.

engineIssue.description: Link or id of the engine issue/PR that tracks or fixed this entry.

kind.description: gap (default, written only when it is not the default): the engine lacked something or got something wrong. efficiency: the engine could have let the AI do the same work in fewer steps, minutes or tokens; it carries waste, evidence, fixType, expectedSaving, appliesTo, measured and saving, measured by the engine from the session transcripts (docs/ENGINE_FEEDBACK.md, "Efficiency feedback").

waste.description: Efficiency entries: what took the time, in engine terms (not the game's names).

evidence.description: Efficiency entries: the spans of the session transcripts (.factoria/ai/sessions) where the waste happened. The engine measures them into `measured`. Steps count from 1: one model call of the built-in agent, one model turn of a CLI agent.

session.description: The transcript's id: its file name in .factoria/ai/sessions without .jsonl.

toStep.description: Last step of the span, inclusive.

fixType.description: Efficiency entries: the fix, cheapest first: doc (a section, or the title and keywords of one that exists), guide (an on-demand topic guide), example, commandOption (an option on a command), newCommand, engineChange (only a candidate for triage).

expectedSaving.description: Efficiency entries: how much of the measured span the fix removes.

share.description: The share of the measured steps, minutes and tokens the fix removes (0.5 = half).

why.description: One line on why the fix removes that share.

appliesTo.description: Efficiency entries: who the fix helps: every-game, genre, feature (one engine feature), this-game (not engine feedback: the report is refused and becomes a project fact).

whyNotCheaper.description: Efficiency entries with fixType commandOption, newCommand or engineChange: why a doc section, a topic guide and an example would not have removed the waste.

searched.description: Efficiency entries about a doc that exists but was not found (findability): the words given to docs.search that did not answer with it.

existingDoc.description: Written by the engine for a findability entry: where the thing is documented (file:line and heading). The fix is that section's title and keywords.

everyStepTokens.description: Efficiency entries: tokens the fix adds to every step of every run (text in AGENTS.md or the system prompt). It must save more than it adds.

measured.description: Efficiency entries, written by the engine from the transcripts: the numbers of all the evidence spans (summed when reports are merged).

steps.description: Model calls (turns of a CLI agent) in the spans.

minutes.description: Time of the spans, tools and waiting included (0.1 minute resolution).

tokens.description: Tokens processed: input + cache + output for the built-in agent, estimated from bytes for a CLI agent.

costUsd.description: Cost in USD; 0 when unknown (a CLI agent writes none).

estimated.description: True when the tokens are estimated from bytes and the cost is not known (a CLI agent).

saving.description: Efficiency entries, written by the engine: measured times the expected share, summed over merged reports. The same fields as measured.

candidate.description: Efficiency entries with fixType engineChange: only a candidate for triage. It goes on the roadmap when the reports that ask for it add up to $1000 or 20 hours across games.

share.description: The generic copy that may be sent to the engine developer: the same gap in engine terms only (components, fields, commands, APIs), with nothing about the game (no names, story, assets, file names or paths). An entry without it is never sent.

title.description: Short noun phrase naming the engine gap.

missing.description: What the engine lacks or gets wrong, in engine terms.

suggestion.description: The engine change that would remove the workaround.

workaround.description: The kind of workaround used, without project details.

reviewed.description: True when the reporter or the user's AI checked against the docs that the gap is real and about the engine.

shared.description: What the engine did with `share` (written by the engine only).

status.description: pending: waiting in the outbox (or for the user's confirmation); sent: the server accepted it; rejected: the server or the sanitizer refused to receive it (see reason); skipped: sharing is off; declined: the server received it and the engine developer rejected the report afterwards (the reason is the developer's, and the entry's status is rejected).

date.description: UTC date of the last change, YYYY-MM-DD.

shareId.description: Id the server gave the report.

occurrences.description: How many times the entry was sent (each send is one occurrence on the server). An entry hit again after it was sent goes again, up to 3, the most the developer's ranking counts.

reason.description: Why it was rejected, declined or skipped.

remote.description: On entries pulled from the feedback server (engine developer only): where the report came from, without identifying anyone.

installKey.description: Opaque key of the installation that sent it (not the installation id).

trust.description: verified: the installation signed in with GitHub.

platform.description: macos, windows, linux, web or other.

reporterKey.description: Opaque key of the GitHub identity that sent it (verified reports only): what `factoria feedback ban --reporter` takes.
